COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 416 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel 
for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A for 
the State/respondent no.1.
3. The revisionist is challenging the order 
dated 13.05.2026 and 16.05.2026 passed by 
learned IInd Additional Civil 
Judge(J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate Roorkee, 
District Haridwar whereby child of one year 
and three months old is ordered to be 
admitted to prison with his mother. It is 
submitted by learned counsel for the 
revisionist that the revisionist being 
grandfather of the child is taking due care of 
child, therefore, it is not in the interest of 
child to admit him to be in prison with 
mother.
4. Let the revisionist along with the child 
and his wife may appear before the 
Chairman of the Child Welfare Committee 
Haridwar, tomorrow at 11.00 a.m., who will 
interact with the revisionist and his wife in 
order to assess the mind of the child then 
apprise to this Court that whether admitting 
the child in prison with the mother is in the 
interest of the child or not.
5. Thereafter, the Chairman shall join 
proceeding through V.C. in the presence of 
revisionist and his wife and child. The 
concerned Jail Authority shall also facilitate  the respondent no. 2 - Smt. Rachna to join 
proceeding through V.C. at 1:00 p.m.
6. List tomorrow at 01.00 p.m. 
7. Till then, Mr. Tumul Nainwal learned 
AGA shall inform to the concerned police 
officials not to act upon the order impugned. 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 02.06.2026
SKS / Nahid

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No.416 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel 
for the revisionist. 
2. Mr. Tumul Nailwal, learned AGA for the 
State. 
3. The Chairman of the Child Welfare 
Committee, Haridwar joined the proceedings 
through video conferencing along with the 
revisionist and the child as well as the 
mother who is in prison. He apprised to this 
Court that the mother of the child is 
agreeable that she may be permitted to 
meet or interact through video conferencing 
with the child every week and after being 
released on bail, permanent custody of the 
child be given to her.
4. When specific query was made from 
the revisionist, he strictly refused to hand 
over the custody of the child to the mother 
after being released on bail. Such an 
attitude of the revisionist cannot be 
accepted since the respondent Smt. Rachna 
is mother of the child, therefore, the child 
cannot be deprived to get love and affection 
from his mother.
5. At this juncture, the respondents 
submit that till such time she is in prison, 
she may be permitted to interact with the  child through video conferencing but 
simultaneously the revisionist has to give an 
undertaking that as and when the revisionist 
shall be released on bail, the custody of the 
child be handed over to the respondent 
mother.
6. Let an affidavit be filed by the 
revisionist positively by 09.06.2026.
7. Put up on 10.06.2026 as fresh.
8. On 10.06.2026, all of them again with 
the Chairman of the Child Welfare 
Committee, Haridwar shall join the 
proceeding through video conferencing.
9. Till then, the revisionist shall not be 
compelled to give the custody of his child to 
the mother, who is in prison. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 03.06.2026 Shiv/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 416 of 2026
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel for 
the revisionist.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned D.A.G. 
alongwith Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned A.G.A. for 
the State.
3. On the last occasion, the Coordinate 
Bench of this Court directed the revisionist to 
file an affidavit to the effect that as and when 
respondent no. 2 is released from jail, then 
the custody of the minor child would be 
handed over to respondent no. 2 by the 
revisionist.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would 
submit that further one week’s time be 
granted to him to file the affidavit in this 
regard. Time so prayed is granted to him.
5. Today, respondent no. 2 is present 
through video conferencing from the office of 
DCPU, Haridwar. The Court interacted with 
her and she has expressed her desire that she 
be permitted to meet her minor child every 
fortnight.
6. Considering the fact that child is only 
one and a half years old and needs care of his 
mother also, therefore, this Court thinks it 
appropriate and directs that the revisionist 
shall bring the child to the office of DCPU, 
Haridwar every fortnight. Superintendant, 
Sub-Jail, Roorkee is directed to ensure that 
respondent no. 2 (Smt. Rachna) be brought to 
the office of DCPU, Haridwar every fortnight. 7. The dates of the visits would be 
intimated by the Chairman, DCPU, Haridwar 
to the Superintendant, Jail Authority as well 
as to the revisionist.
8. List this matter on 29.07.2026.
9. Interim order is extended till the next 
date of listing.
 (Alok Mahra J.) 10.06.2026
Ujjwal

UKHC010094222026
CRLR/416/2026
Chandrapal
--Revisionist
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned counsel 
for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, learned A.G.A. 
for the State.
3. Mr. V.K. Jemini, learned counsel for 
respondent no.2.
4. Learned counsel appearing for 
respondent no.2 would submit that, on 
03.06.2026, before the Coordinate Bench 
of this Court, the revisionist had 
undertaken that, as and when 
respondent no.2, being the mother of the 
minor child, was released from custody, 
he would hand over the custody of the 
minor child to respondent no.2. He would 
further submit that respondent no.2 has 
since been released on bail on 
29.07.2026; however, despite the 
aforesaid undertaking, the revisionist has 
not yet handed over the custody of the 
minor child to respondent no.2.
5. Per contra, learned counsel  appearing for the revisionist would 
submit that the revisionist is ready and 
willing to comply with the undertaking 
given before the Court. He would further 
seek two weeks’ time to obtain 
instructions and to ascertain whether the 
custody of the minor child has been 
handed over to respondent no.2 and 
necessary efforts shall be made by him to 
ensure compliance with the undertaking 
given before the Court.
6. Having regard to the submissions 
advanced by learned counsel for the 
parties and in the interest of justice, two 
weeks’ time, as prayed for by learned 
counsel for the revisionist, is granted to 
obtain instructions and take necessary 
steps in terms of the undertaking given 
before the Court.
7. List this case on 15.10.2026.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 28-09-2026
Mamta
